summary: Evaluate the local cold-plasma relative dielectric tensor from a finite positive frequency, a magnetic field array and a species list. The call returns the tensor alone, as a matrix in the caller's supplied Cartesian basis. Every accepted call returns a finite tensor. The guards reject the whole call with a named exception on the specific failures they name: an explicitly guarded operand, quotient, field magnitude or cyclotron term fails its finite/non-zero requirements; a product of two non-zero factors collapses to zero; a Stix accumulation becomes non-finite; or a contributing species sits at an exact collisionless resonance. A genuine zero field is not one of those failures. At a zero field the represented field magnitude and the cyclotron term are exactly zero by the intended arithmetic and the isotropic result is supported and evaluated; only a represented non-zero field whose magnitude or cyclotron term has collapsed to zero is rejected. A species the caller declares inert is skipped first, and the boundary is representability, not a magnitude cutoff. Other unguarded paths in the function are outside this evidence and are not ruled out; the exact scope is stated in verification.evidence_ceiling. Final tensor assembly evaluates the parallel and perpendicular projections separately; it never forms P-S and adds it back to S. The parallel weights are exact rational B_i*B_j/sum(B_k^2) over the supplied binary64 field; perpendicular diagonals use the other two squared components directly, and perpendicular off-diagonals negate the parallel weight. The Hall term uses the same field norm. Each real/imaginary component is a+b/sqrt(q) with rational a,b,q. Opposite-sign terms use (a^2*q-b^2)/(sqrt(q)*(a*sqrt(q)-b)), retaining the numerator exactly and avoiding cancellation in the denominator; square roots/divisions use 80-digit Decimal arithmetic before one binary64 rounding. An unrepresentable final component raises ColdPlasmaOverflowError for the whole call and a final finite check guards the return. The preceding binary64 Stix accumulation and its conservative guards are unchanged.

capability: Local cold-plasma relative dielectric tensor from frequency, magnetic field and plasma species in the caller's Cartesian basis.
operation: Evaluate the local cold-plasma relative dielectric tensor
discovery.model: Local cold-plasma (Stix) dielectric response with collisional damping; time convention exp(-i omega t).
discovery.geometry: The returned matrix represents the coordinate-free operator S I + (P - S) b b + i D [b]x in the caller-supplied Cartesian basis; the field is a Cartesian vector in the last array axis and no basis change is performed.
discovery.boundary: A zero magnetic field collapses the tensor to the isotropic scalar P times the identity with the off-diagonal term exactly zero; every accepted call returns a finite tensor.

identity.relation: frequency, local magnetic field, and plasma species to the local cold-plasma relative dielectric tensor
identity.definition: Accumulates the Stix cold-plasma scalars S, D and P over the species list with the collision-shifted frequency omega + i*nu, then assembles the coordinate-free tensor as S*I + (P - S)*b b + i*D*[b]x with b the unit magnetic direction. A species entry leaves the loop by one of two routes only. It is skipped when the caller declares it inert -- density_m3 == 0.0 or charge_c == 0.0 -- decided on those two inputs before any operand is formed and before any guard. Otherwise it must contribute, and each explicitly guarded representability failure described below is rejected with ColdPlasmaOverflowError rather than skipped, absorbed or masked. The quantities checked, each where the code forms it, are: the numerator n*q^2; the divisor eps0*m; the plasma contribution n*q^2/(eps0*m); the field magnitude |B|; the signed cyclotron term q|B|/m; the shifted frequency omega + i*nu; the Stix denominator shifted^2 - Omega_c^2; and the four distinct products the three Stix divisions consume -- omega*denominator (shared by S and D), cyclotron*wp2 (the numerator of D), wp2*shifted (the numerator of S) and omega*shifted (the denominator of P). Each is checked where it is formed because an intermediate underflow is evidence about the intermediate and not about the result: wp2 is rescaled by 1/omega**2 before it reaches S, P or D and that denominator can itself be subnormal, and the operands of a product can each be representable while the product is not. The four product guards reject non-finite operands and a product of two non-zero operands that rounds to zero; product overflow itself is left to the downstream accumulation checks. The other named quantities are rejected when not finite, or when exactly zero where a non-zero value is required; no tolerance and no magnitude bound is involved. The field magnitude and the cyclotron term are each required to be non-zero only when the represented field is non-zero, so a genuine zero field is evaluated rather than rejected: |B| and q|B|/m are then zero by the intended arithmetic and the result is the supported isotropic tensor, not a collapse. For each contributing species the accumulation also rejects the call with ColdPlasmaResonanceError if it drives the Stix denominator to exactly zero. Final tensor assembly evaluates the parallel and perpendicular projections separately; it never forms P-S and adds it back to S. The parallel weights are exact rational B_i*B_j/sum(B_k^2) over the supplied binary64 field; perpendicular diagonals use the other two squared components directly, and perpendicular off-diagonals negate the parallel weight. The Hall term uses the same field norm. Each real/imaginary component is a+b/sqrt(q) with rational a,b,q. Opposite-sign terms use (a^2*q-b^2)/(sqrt(q)*(a*sqrt(q)-b)), retaining the numerator exactly and avoiding cancellation in the denominator; square roots/divisions use 80-digit Decimal arithmetic before one binary64 rounding. An unrepresentable final component raises ColdPlasmaOverflowError for the whole call and a final finite check guards the return. The preceding binary64 Stix accumulation and its conservative guards are unchanged.
identity.model: local cold-plasma (Stix) dielectric response with collisional damping; time convention exp(-i*omega*t)
identity.geometry: the returned matrix is the representation, in the caller's supplied Cartesian basis, of the coordinate-free operator S*I + (P - S)*b b + i*D*[b]x built from the supplied field direction; it is not a field-aligned coordinate transform
identity.coordinates: the magnetic field is a Cartesian vector in the last array axis, and the returned matrix is expressed in that same caller-supplied basis; no global coordinate system is assumed and no basis change is performed
identity.boundary: zero magnetic field collapses the tensor to the isotropic scalar P times the identity, with the off-diagonal term set exactly to zero; this is the intended zero-field arithmetic and is supported, not a representability failure. With the field along a coordinate axis the caller's basis and a field-aligned frame coincide, which is a special case and not the general contract
assumptions: The plasma is locally uniform and cold over the scale of the wave; no kinetic or finite-Larmor-radius correction is included.
The cyclotron term is the signed value q|B|/m, so a negative charge carries a negative cyclotron frequency.

Species are supplied in the caller's order and accumulate additively; the operator never reorders them. A species the caller declares inert is skipped and is observationally identical to omitting it, and that is the only route on which an entry leaves the loop without contributing.

Collisions absent is a sufficient condition for Hermiticity, not a necessary one: S, P and D are then real, so i*D*[b]x is purely imaginary and antisymmetric and the tensor is exactly Hermitian at any field strength. A species with zero density or zero charge contributes nothing and cannot make the tensor non-Hermitian however large its collision rate.

An exact collisionless resonance in a contributing species is outside the domain of the cold-plasma relation and is rejected rather than evaluated; the caller must move off resonance, add a collision, or model the resonance kinetically.
The matrix entries are basis-dependent. Only b^H epsilon b, which equals P, and the eigenvalue structure are invariant under a rotation of the caller's basis.

Every input is finite, but a finite input is not automatically representable through the intermediate arithmetic: a large enough frequency, field or density can overflow the plasma contribution, the cyclotron term or the Stix denominator, and a small enough mass or cyclotron term can collapse to exactly zero. Such a call is rejected rather than answered with a masked NaN, an unhandled ZeroDivisionError or a silently dropped contribution, and no magnitude bound is stated.

inputs.name: frequency_hz
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive. A NaN or either infinity is rejected before any arithmetic, so no accepted call can return a non-finite tensor. A finite frequency so large that the intermediate Stix arithmetic overflows is likewise rejected rather than evaluated; no magnitude cutoff is stated, because the value at which a given double-precision arithmetic overflows is a property of the arithmetic rather than of the relation.

inputs.name: magnetic_flux_density_t
inputs.description: Local static magnetic field, with the field vector in the last axis; any leading shape is accepted. The returned matrix is expressed in the Cartesian basis this array is supplied in.
inputs.constraints: Finite, at least one-dimensional, with a final axis of exactly three components. Any point of the array that resonates in a contributing species rejects the whole call. The exact zero field is accepted and evaluated isotropically. A field that is not the zero field but whose represented magnitude is zero is rejected: the magnitude is formed by np.linalg.norm, which squares before it sums, so a field whose only non-zero component is subnormal has every square underflow and would otherwise be classified as the zero field.

inputs.name: species
inputs.description: Iterable of species mappings with density_m3, charge_c, mass_kg, and optional collision_rate_s_inv.
inputs.constraints: Each entry is a mapping with finite values, nonnegative density and collision rate, and strictly positive mass. A collision_hz key is rejected as ambiguous. An empty sequence is legal and yields the vacuum tensor. An entry with exactly zero density or exactly zero charge is skipped before either operand is formed and before every guard, so an inert entry cannot reject a call. The skip is decided on those two inputs and not on the computed product n*q^2: two non-zero inputs can multiply down to zero, and an entry in that state is not inert and is not skipped. An entry the caller declared non-zero is rejected with ColdPlasmaOverflowError when the numerator n*q^2 is not finite; when the divisor eps0*m is not a representable non-zero double -- the case of a finite strictly positive mass so small that eps0*m underflows to zero, which would otherwise raise ZeroDivisionError; when the computed plasma contribution n*q^2/(eps0 m) is not finite or is exactly zero; when the field is not the zero field but its represented magnitude is exactly zero, or the represented cyclotron term q|B|/m is exactly zero beside a non-zero field magnitude; and when any of the four products the three Stix divisions consume is the product of two non-zero operands that rounds to exactly zero. A zero quotient is not a negligible contribution, because the quotient is divided by omega**2 before it reaches the Stix scalars and that denominator can itself be subnormal. Nor is a representable factor evidence that the product is representable. The rejection is a conservative fail-closed boundary on what this arithmetic can represent, not a claim that every rejected entry has an unrepresentable exact contribution.

outputs.name: epsilon_r
outputs.description: Relative dielectric tensor in the caller's supplied Cartesian basis, with the input leading shape plus two trailing tensor axes.
outputs.constraints: Every entry is finite on every accepted call: the accumulation check rejects non-finite S, D or P; the stable final projection and finite gate prevent finite coefficients from producing an accepted NaN/Inf matrix. The small parallel component is preserved across near-resonant finite transverse/parallel scale separation instead of being erased by P-S cancellation. The specifically documented failures reject the whole call with a named exception rather than being evaluated -- a collapsed operand, a zero quotient, a collapsed field magnitude, a collapsed cyclotron term and a collapsed product of two non-zero operands (the four products the three Stix divisions consume) each raise ColdPlasmaOverflowError, and an exact collisionless resonance in a contributing species raises ColdPlasmaResonanceError. A zero-field point is not one of those failures and is returned isotropically. Those named paths are what this asset's evidence audits; other unguarded paths in the function are not ruled out, as verification.evidence_ceiling states. Hermitian at any field strength whenever no species contributes a collision, because i*D*[b]x is then purely imaginary and antisymmetric. A nonzero collision rate on a species that contributes does make it non-Hermitian; a nonzero collision rate on a species with zero density or zero charge does not. The entries are basis-dependent: b^H epsilon b equals P, but the axial entry equals P only when the field lies along that axis.

preconditions: Runtime input checks: the frequency is finite and strictly positive, the field is finite with at least one dimension and exactly three components in its last axis, and each species entry is a mapping of finite density_m3/charge_c/mass_kg with nonnegative density and collision rate and strictly positive mass. These are the only checks that read the shape or the type of an input; a violation raises ValueError before any arithmetic.
The species parameters describe a locally uniform plasma at the field location being evaluated, and the caller has aligned its time convention with exp(-i*omega*t).
The caller reads the returned matrix in the same Cartesian basis it supplied the field in.
No contributing collisionless species sits exactly on its cyclotron resonance at any evaluated field point.

Numerical preconditions, all decided on representability and none on a magnitude: for every contributing species the numerator n*q^2, the divisor eps0*m, the plasma contribution n*q^2/(eps0 m) are representable non-zero doubles; each of the four product guards rejects non-finite operands and exact-zero products of two non-zero factors (a product overflow is assessed by the subsequent accumulation), and the shifted frequency, the Stix denominator and the accumulated S, D and P are finite. The field magnitude and the cyclotron term are required to be non-zero only when the represented field is non-zero: a genuine zero field is supported and evaluated isotropically, and there |B| and q|B|/m are zero by the intended arithmetic rather than by a collapse. The operator rejects rather than rescales when any of them collapses.
supported: Evidence envelope: the regime over which this asset's declared tests measure the relation, which is not a promise over every finite binary64 input. Within it, one or more species accumulating into a single tensor, including species that contribute nothing.
Any leading array shape for the magnetic field, including a scalar field vector and a full spatial grid, with a pointwise call and the corresponding grid row agreeing to about one ulp.

Collisional plasmas through collision_rate_s_inv, including at field values where the collisionless response would be singular; the exact Hermitian collisionless regime at any field strength, and the non-Hermitian contributing-collisional regime.

Zero-field locations, where the represented field magnitude and the cyclotron term are exactly zero by the intended arithmetic and the call is evaluated rather than rejected, collapsing to the isotropic plasma tensor with the off-diagonal term exactly zero.

Near-resonant field values, which return a large finite tensor; a zero-density or zero-charge species sitting exactly on resonance, which is skipped rather than rejected; and a zero-density or zero-charge species in a field whose represented magnitude has collapsed, which is likewise skipped.

Ordinary-range species over the whole representable span of density, charge and mass, evaluated with the operand, field and product checks firing nowhere: over the swept fields and species sets every accepted call is finite and the guards reject nothing, the sweep count asserted to exceed one thousand and the reject count asserted to be exactly zero, so the guards are measured to be transparent on that range rather than merely asserted to be.

The field-overflow boundary the existing guard measures: 1e142 T is accepted and 1e143 T is rejected, because the cyclotron square overflows there; the boundary is the arithmetic's own and is measured by a direct regression rather than asserted.

Stable final projection from represented finite Stix coefficients for axial, near-axis, rotated and mixed-shape fields, including finite cancellation, overflowing P-S and cancellation between symmetric and collisional Hall contributions. Extreme artificial species are arithmetic probes rather than validated experimental plasmas.
excluded: Any rotation of the returned tensor into a different basis, including a field-aligned frame; the caller owns the basis.
Any representation of the resonant response itself; the resonance is rejected, not modelled.

Any numerically rescaled evaluation of the plasma contribution. The operator does not reorder the multiplication to widen the representable range, so an input whose operands, quotient, field magnitude, cyclotron term or Stix product collapses is rejected even when its exact final contribution is representable; a rescaling would change ordinary-range rounding and would need an independent high-precision oracle covering both directions and its own evidence.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for a frequency that is not finite and strictly positive, a magnetic field that is not finite or does not end in three components, a species entry that is not a mapping, a species entry carrying collision_hz instead of collision_rate_s_inv, a species entry missing density_m3/charge_c/mass_kg, or species values with negative density or collision rate, non-positive mass, or non-finite entries.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ColdPlasmaResonanceError, a subclass of ValueError, when any contributing species makes the Stix denominator (omega + i*nu)^2 - Omega_c^2 exactly zero at any field point, naming the offending species index. A species the caller declares inert is skipped before this guard and never triggers it. The rejection is whole-call rather than per-point, because a partially non-finite tensor is not a usable scientific result. The test is exact equality on the computed denominator and not a tolerance, so a near-resonant but non-zero denominator is evaluated normally. A non-zero collision rate on a contributing species removes the singularity, since the denominator's imaginary part is then 2*omega*nu. Raises ColdPlasmaOverflowError, also a subclass of ValueError, when the inputs satisfy the input contract but a quantity the Stix arithmetic forms is not representable. The quantities are checked where the code forms them, and the order matters for the caller only in that the same class and message are raised in every case, so which statement fired is not observable. (1) The numerator n*q^2 is rejected when it is not finite; that stage is defensive rather than reachable at a charge of electronic magnitude, because the quotient after division by eps0*m overflows first. (2) The divisor eps0*m is rejected when it is not a representable non-zero double, which is the subnormal-mass route: a finite positive subnormal mass makes eps0*m underflow to exactly zero, and the division would otherwise raise an undocumented ZeroDivisionError. (3) The plasma contribution n*q^2/(eps0 m) is rejected when it is not finite, and when it is exactly zero. A zero quotient is not a negligible contribution because the quotient is rescaled by 1/omega**2 before it reaches S, P or D and that denominator can itself be subnormal. Two measured witnesses pin the direction: at density_m3 = 1e308, charge_c = 5e-324 and mass_kg = 1e-312 the numerator collapses to exactly zero while the divisor is a representable non-zero denormal, and the exact quotient 2.7568972734915313e-16 moves P by about 315 ulp of one; at density_m3 = 5e-324, charge_c = 1.0, mass_kg = 4e11 and frequency_hz = 5e-163 both operands are representable and positive, the quotient underflows to exactly zero, omega**2 is the subnormal 1e-323, and the exact Stix correction is 0.14134361358724294, so P is 0.8586563864127571 rather than one. (4) The field magnitude is rejected when the field is not the zero field but its represented magnitude is exactly zero, which is the route np.linalg.norm introduces: it squares before it sums, so a field of [5e-324, 0, 0] T has its only square underflow and is represented as the zero field, while the exact norm of that same double is itself a representable double. (5) The cyclotron term q|B|/m is rejected when it is not finite, and when it is exactly zero beside a non-zero field magnitude. An exactly zero cyclotron term at a zero field is correct and is evaluated there; the rejected state is the one where q, |B| and m are finite and non-zero and the quotient is below the double range, so the D contribution it would carry is representable and would otherwise be dropped silently. (6) The shifted frequency, the Stix denominator and the accumulated S, D and P are rejected when they are not finite. The frequency route and the field route are the reachable overflow ones and each has a direct regression: a finite frequency large enough to overflow omega*denominator, and a finite field large enough to overflow the cyclotron square from about 1e143 T. (7) The four distinct products the three Stix divisions consume are rejected when either operand is not finite or when the product of two non-zero operands is exactly zero, because the division would otherwise raise an unhandled ZeroDivisionError or silently zero the contribution the product stood for. A measured witness: at frequency_hz = 2e-109 Hz with field [0, 0, 1e-150] T and a species of density 5e-324 m^-3, charge 1.0 C and mass 112940906737.30191 kg every factor the earlier guards name is finite and non-zero and the product omega*denominator rounds to exactly zero, while the exact D contribution is about 2.2045e-161. A product that overflows to infinity is deliberately not rejected at this stage: finite/inf is a representable zero and inf/inf is a NaN the accumulation check already rejects, so the field band from about 1e140 T is unaffected. The accumulation finiteness check guards the Stix scalars before final assembly and is not a substitute for the checks above, because it observes the accumulator after the division and a finite but wrong quotient passes it. No accepted call raises ZeroDivisionError from any of the four products the three Stix divisions consume; that is not a claim about every other statement in the function. No magnitude bound is stated and none is imposed beyond representability, so an input that is merely large but representable is still evaluated. The accepted set is the set whose intermediates this arithmetic, in the order it forms them, can represent, which is not the set of inputs whose exact contribution is representable: the operator also rejects the band in which an intermediate collapses while the exact final contribution would still be representable, and those bands are disclosed rather than closed. This rejection is whole-call as well, and no partial tensor is returned. Final tensor assembly evaluates the parallel and perpendicular projections separately; it never forms P-S and adds it back to S. The parallel weights are exact rational B_i*B_j/sum(B_k^2) over the supplied binary64 field; perpendicular diagonals use the other two squared components directly, and perpendicular off-diagonals negate the parallel weight. The Hall term uses the same field norm. Each real/imaginary component is a+b/sqrt(q) with rational a,b,q. Opposite-sign terms use (a^2*q-b^2)/(sqrt(q)*(a*sqrt(q)-b)), retaining the numerator exactly and avoiding cancellation in the denominator; square roots/divisions use 80-digit Decimal arithmetic before one binary64 rounding. An unrepresentable final component raises ColdPlasmaOverflowError for the whole call and a final finite check guards the return. The preceding binary64 Stix accumulation and its conservative guards are unchanged.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this operator has no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no tensor.

example.description: Normal use. Evaluate the tensor for an electron-proton plasma in an axial field, confirm the call returns the tensor alone with the documented shape, type and finite entries, confirm that the collisionless tensor is exactly Hermitian, that a contributing collision rate breaks that Hermiticity, and that an exactly resonant zero-density species is skipped rather than rejected. Then confirm the supported zero-field behaviour: the genuine zero field, where the represented field magnitude and the cyclotron term are exactly zero by the intended arithmetic, returns the isotropic tensor with the off-diagonal term exactly zero, and an empty species list returns the vacuum tensor there. Finally the documented failure modes: a non-finite frequency and a malformed field are rejected with ValueError before any arithmetic, a finite frequency whose intermediate arithmetic overflows raises ColdPlasmaOverflowError, and a non-zero field whose represented magnitude has collapsed raises ColdPlasmaOverflowError rather than being evaluated as a zero field.
example.code:
import numpy as np

from scirel.dielectric import (
    ColdPlasmaOverflowError,
    cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor,
)

FREQUENCY_HZ = 60.0e6
ELECTRON = {
    'density_m3': 1.0e19,
    'charge_c': -1.602176634e-19,
    'mass_kg': 9.1093837015e-31,
}
PROTON = {
    'density_m3': 5.0e18,
    'charge_c': 1.602176634e-19,
    'mass_kg': 1.67262192369e-27,
}
AXIAL_FIELD = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.3])

epsilon = cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(
    FREQUENCY_HZ, AXIAL_FIELD, [ELECTRON, PROTON]
)
assert isinstance(epsilon, np.ndarray)
assert epsilon.shape == (3, 3) and epsilon.dtype == np.complex128
assert np.all(np.isfinite(epsilon))
# S on the transverse diagonal, P on the axial entry, an antisymmetric
# purely-imaginary off-diagonal pair and zeros in the axial off-diagonal slots,
# because this field lies along the third coordinate axis.
assert epsilon[0, 0] == epsilon[1, 1]
assert epsilon[0, 1] == -epsilon[1, 0] and epsilon[0, 1].real == 0.0
assert epsilon[0, 2] == 0.0 and epsilon[2, 0] == 0.0

# Collisions absent is sufficient for exact Hermiticity at any field strength.
assert np.max(np.abs(epsilon - epsilon.conj().T)) == 0.0

# A contributing collision rate makes the tensor non-Hermitian.
collisional = cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(
    FREQUENCY_HZ, AXIAL_FIELD,
    [dict(ELECTRON, collision_rate_s_inv=1.0e6), PROTON],
)
assert np.max(np.abs(collisional - collisional.conj().T)) > 0.0

# An exactly resonant species the caller declares inert is skipped, not rejected.
resonant_field_t = (
    2.0 * np.pi * FREQUENCY_HZ * ELECTRON['mass_kg'] / abs(ELECTRON['charge_c'])
)
skipped = cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(
    FREQUENCY_HZ, np.array([0.0, 0.0, resonant_field_t]),
    [dict(ELECTRON, density_m3=0.0)],
)
assert np.array_equal(skipped, cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(
    FREQUENCY_HZ, np.array([0.0, 0.0, resonant_field_t]), []))

# A genuine zero field is supported: the represented field magnitude and the
# cyclotron term are exactly zero there by the intended arithmetic, and the
# result is the isotropic tensor with the off-diagonal term exactly zero.
at_zero = cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(
    FREQUENCY_HZ, np.zeros(3), [ELECTRON, PROTON]
)
assert np.all(np.isfinite(at_zero))
assert at_zero[0, 1] == 0.0 and at_zero[1, 0] == 0.0 and at_zero[0, 2] == 0.0
assert at_zero[0, 0] == at_zero[1, 1] == at_zero[2, 2]
vacuum = cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(FREQUENCY_HZ, np.zeros(3), [])
assert np.array_equal(vacuum, np.eye(3, dtype=complex))

# The documented failures.
for bad_frequency in (float('nan'), float('inf'), -float('inf'), 0.0):
    try:
        cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(bad_frequency, AXIAL_FIELD, [ELECTRON])
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError('a non-finite frequency must be rejected')
try:
    cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(FREQUENCY_HZ, np.array([0.0, 0.0]), [ELECTRON])
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('a field without three components must be rejected')
try:
    cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(1.0e308, AXIAL_FIELD, [ELECTRON])
except ColdPlasmaOverflowError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('an overflowing finite frequency must fail closed')
# [5e-324, 0, 0] T is not the zero field, but np.linalg.norm squares before it
# sums, so every square underflows and its represented magnitude is exactly zero.
assert float(np.linalg.norm(np.array([5e-324, 0.0, 0.0]))) == 0.0
try:
    cold_plasma_dielectric_tensor(
        FREQUENCY_HZ, np.array([5e-324, 0.0, 0.0]), [ELECTRON]
    )
except ColdPlasmaOverflowError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('a collapsed field magnitude must fail closed')
example.expected: A complex128 tensor of shape (3, 3) with finite entries: S on the transverse diagonal, P on the axial entry, an antisymmetric purely-imaginary off-diagonal pair and exactly zero axial off-diagonal slots for this axial field; max |eps - eps^H| == 0 with no collision, and > 0 once a contributing collision rate of 1e6 s^-1 is supplied. An exactly resonant species with zero density is skipped, so the call returns the same tensor as the empty species list at that field. At the genuine zero field the call is evaluated, not rejected: the result is finite and isotropic, with the off-diagonal term exactly zero, and the empty species list returns the identity. ValueError for NaN, for both infinities and for a non-positive frequency, and for a field that does not end in three components. ColdPlasmaOverflowError for a finite frequency of 1e308 Hz, and for the field [5e-324, 0, 0] T, whose represented magnitude is exactly zero while the field itself is not zero.

scope: Runtime input checks: a frequency that is not finite and strictly positive, a field that is not finite or does not end in three components, a species entry that is not a mapping or carries collision_hz, a species entry missing density_m3/charge_c/mass_kg, and species values that are non-finite or negative are each rejected with ValueError before any arithmetic.

That the finite-output statement is true by rejection rather than by assertion: a finite frequency whose intermediate arithmetic overflows is rejected with ColdPlasmaOverflowError instead of returning an all-NaN tensor, and a rejected call produces no partial tensor.

That no accepted finite species input leaks ZeroDivisionError: a finite positive subnormal mass_kg makes the divisor eps0*m underflow to exactly zero and is rejected with the same named ColdPlasmaOverflowError, asserted to be a ValueError subclass.

That the operand and quotient checks are conservative fail-closed boundaries on representability and not magnitude cutoffs: the numerator check fires on an exact zero or a non-finite value, the divisor check fires on a product of two finite doubles that is not a representable non-zero number, and neither states a threshold or a bound. The two underflow witnesses for the plasma contribution -- a collapsed numerator with a representable divisor, and a zero quotient of two representable positive operands -- are direct regressions whose exact quotients are re-derived from exact rational arithmetic over the same doubles and pinned as literals.

That the operand, field and product checks do not disturb the inert skip: a species the caller declares inert with zero density or zero charge is still skipped rather than rejected even when its mass is subnormal, its numerator or quotient would collapse, or the field's represented magnitude has collapsed, because the skip is decided on those inputs before any operand is formed and before every guard. It is the only route on which a species leaves the loop without contributing.

That both reachable overflow routes are covered by direct regressions: the frequency route, where a finite frequency overflows the shared Stix denominator product, and the field route, where a finite field overflows the cyclotron square from about 1e143 T. The plasma contribution is formed in stages, so both its operands are checked before the division; the numerator overflow stage is defensive rather than exercised, because at a charge of electronic magnitude the quotient after division by eps0*m overflows first. That distinction is asserted in the test body so the wording cannot drift.
That every accepted call returns a finite tensor, swept over a few dozen field configurations and several species sets rather than a single witness.

That the checks are transparent wherever they accept: over the swept fields and species sets -- two hundred fields uniform in [-2, 2] and fifty log-spaced fields over twelve decades, crossed with six species sets -- every accepted call is finite and the guards reject nothing, the sweep asserted to exceed one thousand accepted calls and the reject count asserted to be exactly zero. The guards are deliberately not claimed to be a no-op on every input that an alternative formulation evaluated to a finite tensor: the measured non-no-op bands -- the cyclotron-square overflow above about 1e143 T and the collapsed operand, quotient, product, cyclotron and field-magnitude routes -- are measured and disclosed rather than left implicit.

That no magnitude cutoff was introduced: the rejection message states no bound, and each guard is representability rather than a chosen maximum or minimum. The existing field-overflow boundary is measured at its own edge on ordinary calls -- 1e142 T is accepted and 1e143 T is rejected -- and a small field whose cyclotron term is a representable non-zero double is accepted.

That a species the caller declares inert is skipped before the resonance guard: a zero-density and a zero-charge species each evaluate at the exact resonance where a contributing species would be rejected, and are asserted np.array_equal to the empty-species vacuum tensor at collision rates from 0 to 1e15.

That the resonance guard is narrowed rather than weakened: a contributing species at the same point still raises the named ColdPlasmaResonanceError, and the reported index is the contributing species'. The sibling conductivity relation guards the same denominator with the same exact-zero test; the test body re-derives that closed form rather than loading the sibling.

The coordinate contract, measured rather than asserted: b^H epsilon b equals P on axis and off it, the axial entry is measurably not P for a tilted field, and eps @ b differs from S b off axis -- so the matrix is the operator in the caller's basis and not a field-aligned representation. The module and function docstrings are asserted not to claim a field-aligned frame.

The carried formulation's arithmetic is unchanged: a bit-identity comparison over 600 non-resonant inputs, measured outside this repository, supports that claim and is not part of this contract's test evidence. The non-finite-frequency rejection is a documented divergence rather than a change to that arithmetic.

Independent closed-form agreement for the S, D and P entries assembled in the test body, for a single species and for a mixed collisional multi-species call; and the sign convention of the cyclotron argument, re-derived in the test body from the same relation the module implements rather than by loading the conductivity relation -- the module's own reading, the field magnitude q|B|/m, recovers the tensor to machine precision at both field signs and both collision rates, while the signed projection q*B_z/m measures a 1.7e-2 relative mismatch when the axial field is negative, which is what makes the equivalence a convention about the argument rather than an identity of magnitudes.

That the call returns the tensor and nothing else, with the time convention and the model label held as module constants; that the Hermiticity statement is two separate claims, exactness at two nonzero field magnitudes and both field signs when no species contributes a collision, and the counterexamples that refute 'any nonzero collision rate breaks it'; and zero-field isotropy, the inherited one-ulp grid artefact, and representative input-contract rejections.

That one statement covers both plasma-contribution underflow routes and the caller cannot tell them apart: a numerator that collapses to zero makes the computed plasma contribution zero, and a numerator that is not finite is rejected before the division, so the quotient test subsumes the numerator-zero case rather than being carried beside it. The module source is asserted to contain the quotient test and no numerator-zero test, so the rule is stated once.

That the refuted readings of a zero quotient are gone from the module text, including the denormal-numerator/denormal-divisor residual band, which is refuted because the quotient of two positive subnormal doubles is at least about 2.22e-16 and cannot round to zero. The check allows a refuted sentence to appear only as a quotation followed in the same breath by the sentence that refutes it.

That the collapsed-product witnesses are direct regressions that discriminate rather than merely pass: every factor the earlier guards name is re-measured as a representable non-zero double, the product under test is re-measured to be exactly zero while its exact rational value is strictly positive, and the discarded contribution is proved representable from exact rational arithmetic over the same doubles -- standard-library Fraction only, never a high-precision runtime dependency and never a rescaled evaluation. That an unguarded formulation still leaks the undocumented ZeroDivisionError or silently zeroes the contribution is not measured here; these regressions concern the unchanged Stix arithmetic the guards protect. Final assembly has its own exact-projection recovery and independent high-precision oracle, described below.

That all three Stix accumulations are audited for the multiplication-before-division class over the four products the three divisions consume rather than over the three divisions, so the count of divisions is not confused with the count of products. Three of the four products have an independent witness; the fourth, omega * shifted, is asserted to be guarded in the module source, and this revision presents no independent witness for it and claims none either way.

That the product guard is exact and states no bound: it rejects a product of two finite non-zero doubles that rounds to exactly zero, whatever the magnitudes, and it accepts every product that is a representable non-zero number however small, so it is representability and not a chosen floor. A product that is exactly zero because an operand is exactly zero is accepted by the helper, which decides the product and not where its operands came from; no contributing species reaches the helper with a cyclotron operand that is zero because of an underflow, because the field and cyclotron guards reject that state first, so the zero cyclotron operand the helper accepts is the genuine zero-field one. A non-finite operand is rejected rather than silently accepted, which is why the operands are tested before the product. A product that overflows to infinity is deliberately not rejected.

That the field-magnitude and cyclotron guards are direct regressions on the counterexamples that motivated them: for a field whose only non-zero component is subnormal the represented field is asserted non-zero and its represented norm exactly zero, while the exact norm of that same double is asserted itself a representable double; and for the cyclotron route the represented cyclotron term is asserted exactly 0.0 beside a non-zero field magnitude while the exact term over the same represented doubles is non-zero. That a formulation without these guards answers the zero-field branch for the first and returns a finite tensor with a zeroed off-diagonal entry for the second is not measured here; the tests assert the rejected state itself.

That the correction distinguishes the two cases rather than rejecting zero fields: a genuine zero-field call carries the same species as the cyclotron-route counterexample and differs only in the field, both have a represented cyclotron term of exactly 0.0, and the first is rejected while the second is evaluated and returns the isotropic tensor with the off-diagonal term exactly zero. What the guards key on is the represented field and not the cyclotron term alone.

That the two field guards come after the inert skip and are transparent wherever they accept: a species the caller declares inert is skipped rather than rejected on a field whose represented magnitude has collapsed, and its result is asserted np.array_equal to the empty-species vacuum tensor at both the collapsed field and the true zero field; and over the same fields and species sets as the earlier sweeps every accepted call is finite with no rejection, the sweep count asserted to exceed one thousand and the reject count asserted to be exactly zero. The guards fire nowhere on the swept ordinary-range inputs, and they test exact zero and finiteness only, so no tolerance or threshold appears in either.

Final assembly: the three axial finite-Stix witnesses fail without the final projection; the current assembly returns finite axial and rotated tensors, with Decimal400/480 projection agreement at the declared normwise tolerance. A separate two-species collisional witness has finite Stix components but a genuinely unrepresentable final matrix component and is rejected, including a mixed leading-shape call. Forty-eight ordinary arbitrary-direction and collision-rate cases agree with a separately solved Cartesian3x3 cold momentum system, evaluated by Decimal400/480 Gauss-Jordan rather than Stix/projector formulas; the comparison tolerance is unchanged.

A finite-only fallback is scientifically rejected by three preserved near-resonant axial cases: P=0.19999999999999996 returned 0.25. The declared final assembly passes the same 1e-14 relative assertion and 96 near-axis scale/collision cases with independent Decimal 400/480 orthonormal field-frame rotation, including the small diagonal on its own scale. Six rotated collisional cases verify tiny real symmetric/Hall cancellation residuals componentwise at 1e-14 relative tolerance. Thirty-six additional mixed-scale cases agree with the independent Cartesian 3x3 momentum system, supplementing 48 such cases. The near-pole rotation oracle binds the already represented Stix coefficients to isolate final-assembly accuracy; it is not a new proof of near-resonant Stix accuracy.
verification.evidence_ceiling: This document separates three things, and the separation is the contract. (1) The runtime input shape and type checks the operator performs are listed in applicability.preconditions and failure_semantics.invalid_input: they read the shape and the type of the inputs, they raise ValueError before any arithmetic, and they are the only checks the operator makes about what the caller passed. (2) The scientific applicability and numerical evidence envelope the declared tests actually measure is listed in applicability.supported: it is the regime over which the relation has been shown to be evaluated as intended and over which the guards are transparent, and it is not a proof over every finite binary64 input. (3) Known behaviour outside that envelope is listed in applicability.excluded and in known_limitations below. Within the envelope this asset establishes the cold-plasma tensor identity, its equivalence to the conductivity formulation, the stated sign convention, the Hermiticity structure of the returned tensor, the exact-resonance rejection contract and the set of species it applies to, the basis the returned matrix is expressed in, and that every accepted call returns a finite tensor -- the last by rejecting a finite input whose intermediate arithmetic is not representable rather than by asserting a bound. It does not establish that every path that could mask a NaN or leak a ZeroDivisionError is closed, and it does not establish that every arithmetic intermediate is guarded. It does not establish that the cold-plasma model is adequate at any particular frequency or collisionality for a physical device, does not establish where the representability boundary lies beyond the specific witnesses a regression pins, and does not establish the physically correct response at or near a resonance, which is a kinetic question outside this asset's scope. In particular it does not establish that the accepted set is the largest one on which this relation could be evaluated: the guards reject on the representability of the operands, of the field magnitude, of the cyclotron term, of the four products and of the quotient this arithmetic forms in this order, and the band in which an intermediate collapses while the exact final contribution would still be representable is disclosed rather than closed. The measured witnesses of that band -- a collapsed numerator whose exact quotient is 2.7568972734915313e-16, a collapsed quotient whose exact Stix correction is 0.14134361358724294, a collapsed shared denominator product whose exact D is about 2.2045e-161, a collapsed S numerator whose exact S correction is 1.2351641146031161e-23, and a collapsed cyclotron term whose exact D is 1.129409067373019e-131 -- are all rejected rather than dropped, and each is pinned by a direct regression in the declared test file. No residual band is claimed to be open on the ground that the operands are denormal: the quotient of two positive subnormal doubles is at least about 2.22e-16 and cannot round to zero, and a zero quotient of any two positive representable operands is rejected here. A numerically rescaled evaluation carrying wp2/omega**2 as a single ratio, backed by an independent high-precision oracle covering both the underflow and the overflow direction, could represent inputs the current guards reject; it is deliberately not introduced, and no such oracle is claimed. A finite return is not evidence that the call is inside the relation's scientific domain. Final tensor assembly evaluates the parallel and perpendicular projections separately; it never forms P-S and adds it back to S. The parallel weights are exact rational B_i*B_j/sum(B_k^2) over the supplied binary64 field; perpendicular diagonals use the other two squared components directly, and perpendicular off-diagonals negate the parallel weight. The Hall term uses the same field norm. Each real/imaginary component is a+b/sqrt(q) with rational a,b,q. Opposite-sign terms use (a^2*q-b^2)/(sqrt(q)*(a*sqrt(q)-b)), retaining the numerator exactly and avoiding cancellation in the denominator; square roots/divisions use 80-digit Decimal arithmetic before one binary64 rounding. An unrepresentable final component raises ColdPlasmaOverflowError for the whole call and a final finite check guards the return. The preceding binary64 Stix accumulation and its conservative guards are unchanged. The final-assembly evidence is bounded by the limitations just stated; independent review and public redistribution are separate decisions.
known_limitations: Outside the evidence envelope: the operator returns a finite array for any input whose intermediates this arithmetic can represent, and that is not by itself evidence that the call is scientifically validated. Nothing here establishes that the cold-plasma model is adequate for a particular device, frequency or collisionality, and the returned finite tensor must not be read as an endorsement of the model at that operating point.
The model is strictly cold and local; warm-plasma and kinetic corrections are out of scope.

The non-finite-frequency rejection is a deliberate divergence from a formulation that accepts NaN and positive infinity and returns an all-NaN tensor. The carried arithmetic is otherwise unchanged. The divergence is taken because a public contract cannot return an all-NaN tensor from an accepted call.

Skipping a zero-contribution species is a deliberate divergence from a formulation that rejects the whole call for such a species at exact resonance and otherwise raises ZeroDivisionError, so neither behaviour is a contract this asset can inherit.

The overflow rejection is a divergence from behaviour that returned an all-NaN tensor for a finite frequency whose intermediate arithmetic overflows and a finite leading-order tensor for a finite field that overflows the cyclotron square. It is not a narrowing of the input domain by a chosen magnitude: the guard tests representability, so no bound is published. Because the guard tests the intermediate rather than the result, it also rejects a band of field magnitudes, about 1e143 T to 1e297 T, for which the leading-order tensor would still be representable; the finite value there comes from x / inf = 0 dropping the species contribution, not from evaluating it.

The guards make the finite-output statement true by rejection rather than by a bound. A caller that needs to know in advance whether an extreme input is representable must derive the condition from the relation and its own arithmetic, or catch ColdPlasmaOverflowError. In particular the operator does not rescale the plasma contribution to widen the representable range, so it rejects some inputs whose exact final contribution is representable -- the band in which n*q^2 collapses while eps0*m does not, the band in which the quotient collapses while the Stix correction wp2/omega**2 would still be representable, the band in which one of the four products the three Stix divisions consume collapses while the contribution it carries would still be representable, and the band in which the field magnitude or the cyclotron term collapses while the exact contribution would still be representable. That is a conservative fail-closed boundary on what this arithmetic can represent, and not a claim that every rejected input has an unrepresentable exact contribution. Closing it would require a rescaled evaluation backed by an independent high-precision oracle covering both the overflow and the underflow direction, which this revision deliberately does not introduce.

The singularity test is exact equality on the computed denominator rather than a tolerance, so a caller sampling densely near a resonance must apply its own proximity criterion; this asset deliberately does not choose one, because near-resonant values must remain distinguishable from the singular point. The physically correct resonant response is not represented at all, since it requires a kinetic treatment this asset excludes.
Rejection is whole-call: for an array field, a single resonant or unrepresentable point in a contributing species discards the tensor at every other point as well.

A field supplied as a one-dimensional vector and the same field supplied as one row of a grid differ by about one ulp, because numpy evaluates scalar and array complex division by different paths. The bound is asserted in the tests and follows from numpy's evaluation paths rather than from this extension.
The returned matrix is basis-dependent. A caller that needs the field-aligned representation must rotate it; this asset performs no basis change and documents no convention for one.

The fourth product omega * shifted, the denominator of P, is guarded by the same rule as the other three Stix products but has no independent witness in the declared test file. The guard is exact and states no bound, so nothing about the contract depends on which of the four products a given input collapses in.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.

The final projection does not recover information already lost in the unchanged binary64 Stix coefficients or expand their conservative representability boundaries. A rounded Cartesian matrix can remain ill-conditioned when a subsequent consumer projects a much smaller eigenresponse from large entries; that is distinct from the fixed loss of a representable matrix component during assembly. Exact rational coefficients and stable80-digit algebraic evaluation add per-point runtime cost; timings are bounded measurements, not a universal performance guarantee. Extreme witnesses establish arithmetic behavior, not cold-model applicability to artificial species.
